English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Hebrew לוּז (luz, “almond”).

Noun

[edit]

luz

English Wikipedia has an article on:
luz (bone)
Wikipedia
  1. A small bone in the human spinal column, believed in Muslim and Jewish traditions to be the indestructible bone from which the body will be rebuilt at the time of resurrection.
  2. The almond tree

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese luz, from Latin lūcem, from Proto-Italic *louks, from the Proto-Indo-European root *lewk- (“white; light; bright”). Compare Portuguese luz.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • IPA(key): /ˈluθ/ [ˈluθ]
  • IPA(key): (standard) /ˈluθ/ [ˈluθ]
  • IPA(key): (seseo) /ˈlus/ [ˈlus]

 
  • Rhymes: -uθ
  • Rhymes: -uθ
  • Rhymes: -us

  • Hyphenation: luz

Noun

[edit]

luz f (plural luces)

  1. light
  2. daylight

Derived terms

[edit]
  • lucecú
  • luceiro

Related terms

[edit]
  • lucir

References

[edit]
  • Seoane, Ernesto Xosé González; Granja, María Álvarez de la; Agrelo, Ana Isabel Boullón (2006–2022), “luz”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios do galego medieval [Dictionary of dictionaries of Medieval Galician] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Barreiro, Xavier Varela; Guinovart, Xavier Gómez (2006–2018), “luz”, in Corpus Xelmírez: corpus lingüístico da Galicia medieval [Corpus Xelmírez: linguistic corpus of Medieval Galicia] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “luz”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, Ernesto Xosé González Seoane, María Álvarez de la Granja, editors (2003–2018), “luz”, in Tesouro informatizado da lingua galega (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Rosario Álvarez Blanco, editor (2014–2024), “luz”, in Tesouro do léxico patrimonial galego e portugués (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega, →ISSN

Polish

[edit]
Polish Wikipedia has an article on:
luz
Wikipedia pl

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • lus (Central Greater Poland)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Polish *luz (attested in luzem), from Middle High German lōs.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈlus/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -us
  • Syllabification: luz

Noun

[edit]

luz m inan (diminutive luzik)

  1. spacious place
  2. slack (part of something that has no strain upon it)
  3. clearance (distance between moving parts of a machine)
  4. (colloquial) free time, leisure
  5. (colloquial) ease (freedom from effort, difficulty or hardship)
    Synonym: swoboda
  6. (colloquial) margin (in machine learning: distance from the data point to a decision boundary)
    Synonym: marża
  7. (colloquial, automotive) idle (running a vehicle's engine when the vehicle is not in motion)
    Synonym: bieg jałowy

Declension

[edit]
Declension of luz
singular plural
nominative luz luzy
genitive luzu luzów
dative luzowi luzom
accusative luz luzy
instrumental luzem luzami
locative luzie luzach
vocative luzie luzy

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese luz, from Latin lūcem, from Proto-Italic *louks, from the Proto-Indo-European root *lewk- (“white; light; bright”). Doublet of lux. Compare Galician luz.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈlu(j)s/ [ˈlu(ɪ̯)s]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈlu(j)s/ [ˈlu(ɪ̯)s]
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /ˈlu(j)ʃ/ [ˈlu(ɪ̯)ʃ]
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈluʃ/

  • Audio (São Paulo):(file)
  • Rhymes: (Brazil) -us, (Portugal, Rio de Janeiro) -uʃ
  • Hyphenation: luz

Noun

[edit]

luz f (plural luzes)

  2. light (medium within which vision is possible)
    • 1915, Alberto Caeiro (Fernando Pessoa), “É noite”:
      É noite. A noite é muito escura. Numa casa a uma grande distancia. Brilha a luz d'uma janella.
      It's night. The night is very dark. In a house a great distance away. The light from a window shines.
  4. light; light source (object that emits light)
  6. (figurative) light; enlightenment (knowledge about things as they really are)
  7. (colloquial) electricity
Quotations
[edit]

For quotations using this term, see Citations:luz.

[edit]

  • dar à luz
  • luz-em-cu
Related terms
[edit]
  • lúcido
  • lucífero
  • luzerna
  • lúzio
  • luzir

[edit]

luz

  1. inflection of luzir:
    1. third-person singular present indicative

Spanish

[edit]
Spanish Wikipedia has an article on:
luz
Wikipedia es

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Spanish luz, from Latin lūcem, from Proto-Italic *louks, from Proto-Indo-European *léwks (“light”). Compare the borrowed doublet lux.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈluθ/ [ˈluθ] (Spain, Equatorial Guinea)
  • IPA(key): /ˈlus/ [ˈlus] (Latin America, Philippines)
  • Rhymes: -uθ (Spain, Equatorial Guinea)
  • Rhymes: -us (Latin America, Philippines)
  • Syllabification: luz

Noun

[edit]

luz f (plural luces)

  1. light
    la luz extinguida
    the extinguished light
  2. (anatomy) lumen
  3. (figurative, usually in the plural) brightness, intelligence
    Vas a llegar con menos luces.
    You're going to get there with less intellect.
  4. (figurative) focus, point of view, understanding
    Debes verlo bajo una nueva luz.
    You must see it from a new point of view.
  5. (electricity) electric power
    Se fue la luz.
    The lights went out. (There is a blackout.)
  6. (architecture) span
